I have been traveling for work, conferences, and weddings for almost a month. Thankfully, it rains enough in Louisiana that my plants don't get thirsty, but they have been neglected.

Monday night when we flew home, there were about 20 noodle beans that needed picking, most of which had dehydrated on the vine or had gotten too big to eat. I saved the seeds from the big ones and shriveled ones, and the few that were smaller and tender, we ate. I cooked them in olive oil + sesame oil, salt and pepper, with fresh squeezed lime juice, fresh basil and mint, and chili paste. Here's a collage of the veggies, salad, and the beans I saved from the shriveled pods that are currently drying on a paper plate.

When we got home it was already dark, but Tuesday morning I took some pictures of how the noodle bean and mirliton vines have jumped from the trellis into the tree above them. The mirliton went first, with the noodle beans climbing around it, and they've reached all the way to the top of the tree. Some pictures:

Noodle bean vines on trellis.
